public_rationale: The condition was met: OpenAI released GPT-5 on 7 August 2025. Marcus forecast that it would not meet AGI criteria of the kind he had set out, such as his 2022 test requiring at least three of five demanding tasks. On the eve of launch, OpenAI's CEO said that by most definitions of AGI, GPT-5 was still missing important things, including continuous learning. I found no credible evaluation saying GPT-5 met Marcus's tasks or counted as AGI. The developer's own statement settles the plain reading in Marcus's favor.
limitations: No task-by-task test of GPT-5 against the five criteria was found. The result rests on the developer's general admission.
The result depends on reading 'criteria for AGI' as the 2022 five-task test or similar.

our_interpretation: Condition: OpenAI releases a model named GPT-5.

His previously stated criteria are read as his 2022 five-task test (understand movies, understand novels, cook in any kitchen, reliably write 10,000+ lines of bug-free code, convert arbitrary math proofs to symbolic form), which required at least three of five, and similar AGI criteria.
Plain reading: GPT-5 at release would not qualify as AGI by criteria of that kind.
criteria.support_condition: After GPT-5's release, its developer or credible evaluators find that it falls short of AGI or of Marcus-type criteria.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evaluation shows GPT-5 meets at least three of Marcus's five tasks, or is widely accepted as AGI.
